title: 'Cannot represent' overstates a search-range choice, and the paper's own trivial baseline proves it
quote: None of these can represent, much less estimate, a negative confidence--correctness association.
explanation: What the evidence supports is that published protocols restrict their tuning range to non-negative exponents or temperatures. The paper's own SignGrid-dev is the same $c^{\gamma}$ family with the sign released, and it reaches the signed test-set oracle across the whole negative half-axis (1.000 at kappa = -0.6 and -0.4, 0.993 at -0.2, 0.892 at -0.1). The barrier is therefore one sign bit in a hyperparameter grid, not the representational limit of the weight family. Correcting this resizes the contribution honestly rather than removing it: from a capability no published scheme has, to a capability no published scheme searches for, plus an estimator that finds it without labels. The universal quantifiers ('Every published weighting scheme', 'None of these') also carry no stated search scope; the hedge 'to the author's knowledge' appears once in the Introduction and is dropped in the abstract and Related Work.
allowed_wording: of the confidence-weighted self-consistency protocols surveyed here, all restrict the exponent or temperature to non-negative values, so a negative association is never searched for and, being unmeasured, cannot be acted on
forbidden_wording: None of these can represent, much less estimate, a negative confidence--correctness association.
the possibility that the channel is \emph{anti-correlated} with correctness is not representable

title: The one rank-based comparator in the bibliography is filed as a budget refinement and never run
quote: Weighted variants \cite{li2023diverse,borda2025} and early-stopping families \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive,li2024escape} refine the budget
explanation: By the paper's own bibliography, borda2025 is Kang, Zhao and Song, 'Scalable best-of-N selection for large language models via self-certainty', NeurIPS 2025: an aggregation/selection rule over a self-certainty signal, not a budget mechanism, and the author's chosen citation key suggests awareness that it aggregates by rank. Contribution C1's headline property is rank-based invariance, and the adversarial oracle is explicitly restricted to raw-value policies, so no published rank-based aggregator appears anywhere in the baseline set. The comparator best placed to contest C1 is cited once, in a subordinate clause, with no characterization. Either state why its rank aggregation does not already confer monotone invariance, or add it to Table II.

title: The bibliography already contains the standard remedy for the paper's self-declared worst failure, uncited
quote:
a dominant
wrong cluster that is semantically tight but carries no verbatim signature, so
deduplication has nothing to collapse
explanation: The unguarded failure mode is a consequence of a design choice: deduplication runs on 'single-linkage duplicate groups on the lexical-similarity channel at $0.95$', so a semantically tight paraphrase cluster is invisible to it. Semantic-equivalence clustering is the standard published response, and kuhn2023semantic (Kuhn, Gal and Farquhar, semantic uncertainty) sits in the bibliography as an uncited \bibitem. Calling the failure 'unguarded' without noting that the guard exists in the literature, and in the paper's own reference list, understates what a revision could do about it. Cite it either as the remedy not adopted, with a reason, or as future work.

title: The sibling negative result is offered as evidence but cannot be checked, and de-anonymizes in Related Work
quote: \textbf{Honest sibling result.} A preceding system by the author (RLEV-VoI, redundancy-discounted voting with value-of-information stopping) was evaluated under the same falsification discipline and \emph{failed} it
explanation: This paragraph does real argumentative work: the Conclusion offers the falsification protocol as the paper's most portable contribution on the strength of 'having already killed one of the author's own systems'. Yet there is no \cite, arXiv identifier, report, or artifact pointer, so the reader cannot verify the killed system, the discipline applied to it, or the deduplication baseline that dominated it. As placed, it also identifies the author inside Related Work, which matters if the target track is double-blind. Move it to the Limitations section or an appendix with a citable pointer.
